issues.title: Inconsistent Chinese translation for 'Name' field across namespaces
issues.description: The PR updates the Chinese translation for 'Name' from '称呼' to '姓名' across multiple translation files to ensure consistency. However, this change creates a cross-namespace inconsistency issue. In ghost.json, line 31 shows 'Name' translated as '名字' (first name), while in portal.json line 117 it's translated as '名称' (generic name/title). This inconsistency will confuse Chinese users when they see different terminology for the same 'Name' field between email templates (using ghost namespace) and the portal UI (using portal namespace). The correct translation should be '姓名' (full name) consistently across both files as intended by the original PR.

issues.title: Missing interpolation variable in newsletter unsubscribe message
issues.description: The translation for the key '{memberEmail} will no longer receive {newsletterName} newsletter.' in portal.json is missing the {newsletterName} interpolation variable. The Chinese translation only includes '{memberEmail}将不会再收到新闻信。' which omits the newsletter name placeholder. This means when users unsubscribe from a specific newsletter, they won't see which newsletter they're unsubscribing from, leading to confusion and potential accidental unsubscriptions. The translation should include both {memberEmail} and {newsletterName} variables to match the English source and maintain functional parity.

issues.title: Translation inconsistency for 'Enter your name' field across UI contexts
issues.description: The PR introduces an inconsistency in the Chinese translation for the 'Enter your name' input field. In portal.json line 71, it's translated as '输入您的名字' (enter your first name), which suggests only a first name is needed. However, based on the context of Ghost's user registration and profile system, and the fact that the 'Name' field itself should be '姓名' (full name), this creates a mismatch between what the label asks for ('名字' - first name) and what the system actually expects ('姓名' - full name). This can cause user confusion during registration and profile completion, potentially leading to incomplete or incorrectly formatted name entries.

issues.title: Deletion of comments.json breaks comments-ui build for Chinese locale
issues.description: The PR deletes ghost/i18n/locales/zh/comments.json, but this file is required by the comments-ui application build configuration. In apps/comments-ui/vite.config.mts line 56, the Vite build explicitly declares dynamicRequireTargets for comments.json across all SUPPORTED_LOCALES, including 'zh'. When the build system attempts to bundle the Chinese locale translations, it will fail because the required comments.json file no longer exists. This will break the build process for the comments-ui application or cause runtime failures when users try to view comments in Chinese.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25696 - Align zh translations with China mainland terminology.
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
The PR is meant to be a text-only zh-CN wording pass across three locale files: ghost.json, portal.json and comments.json. It also fills in the one empty "Subscription details" translation. The stated intent is consistent 评论/名字 terminology and more natural subscription and email-preference copy, with no new files.

The head commit does not match that description. comments.json is deleted outright (74 lines removed), so none of the comment-related zh strings survive. The i18n layer falls back to en, so Chinese users would see English comment UI. Beyond that, the changes in ghost.json and portal.json are mostly sound, but a few edits drop a placeholder, flip the tense of a status label, and leave "Name" and "email" terminology inconsistent with the stated goal. I would not merge until the comments.json deletion is resolved and the placeholder regression is fixed.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The PR deletes ghost/i18n/locales/zh/comments.json entirely, which contradicts the description's claim that the file was refined. That removes every zh comment translation, and the configured fallbackLng of 'en' means Chinese members will see English comment UI. A translation also drops the {newsletterName} placeholder, so the message no longer says which newsletter was unsubscribed. These need fixing before merge; the terminology inconsistencies are worth addressing but are not blockers.

architecture.overview:
Ghost's admin and member-facing UI text is keyed by English source strings. Each locale directory under ghost/i18n/locales/<lang>/ holds JSON files (ghost.json, portal.json, comments.json, and others), and the i18n library in ghost/i18n/lib/i18n.js loads them with i18next. Its fallbackLng is configured to fall back to 'en' when a key is missing from the active locale.

This PR touches only the zh locale files. It rewrites many values in ghost.json and portal.json, adds the previously empty 'Subscription details' value, and deletes comments.json. Because the key lookup falls back to English, a deleted file does not fail loudly; it silently replaces every zh comment string with English text.
steps: Entry point: the i18n library loads the locale JSON files for the requested language from ghost/i18n/locales/<lang>/ and uses 'en' as the fallback.
ghost.json (zh) changes: subscription wording moves from 会籍 to 订阅, the 'Comment' and 'Name' terms are updated, and 'Subscription details' gets its first translation.

portal.json (zh) changes: a number of portal strings are reworded. Some edits drop or alter placeholders such as {newsletterName}, and 'Name' and 'email' terms are no longer consistent with ghost.json.
comments.json (zh): the whole file is deleted in this PR, so all comment UI keys fall back to English at runtime.
Net effect: text-only data change with no code or API impact, but the deletion is a functional regression for zh comment UI.

findings.title: comments.json deleted, removing all zh comment translations
findings.fixPrompt: In the Ghost repo, `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/comments.json` is deleted by this PR, but the PR is meant to refine its zh-CN copy. Restore the file from the base commit (96253df) and apply the intended wording changes: consistent 评论 and 名字 terms, and clearer load/show hints. Keep the existing key set so that no comment UI string falls back to English. Verify that every key in `ghost/i18n/locales/en/comments.json` still has a zh value.

findings.title: {newsletterName} placeholder dropped from unsubscribe message
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/portal.json` line 9, the value for the key `{memberEmail} will no longer receive {newsletterName} newsletter.` no longer contains the `{newsletterName}` placeholder. Restore the placeholder in the Chinese value while keeping the reworded phrasing, for example `{memberEmail}将不会再收到{newsletterName}的新闻信。`. Confirm that the value still contains both `{memberEmail}` and `{newsletterName}`, matching the English key.

findings.title: "Name" translated inconsistently across locale files
findings.fixPrompt: Make the zh-CN translation of the English key `Name` consistent across `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/ghost.json` (line 31) and `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/portal.json` (line 117). The PR goal is 名字, so change the portal.json value from 名称 back to 名字 and check for other uses of 名称 for name fields in the zh portal and comments files.

findings.title: Status label changed from present to future tense
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/portal.json` line 213, the zh value for `You're not receiving emails` was changed to a future-tense phrasing (`您将不会收到邮件。`). Restore a present-tense status meaning consistent with the neighbouring key `You're currently not receiving emails` on line 212, for example `您当前不会收到邮件。`. Keep the wording otherwise unchanged.

findings.title: Mixed 邮件 and 邮箱 terminology in portal.json
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/portal.json`, align the use of 邮件 (email messages) and 邮箱 (email address) across the updated strings. Use 邮箱 only when the string refers to an address (for example lines 199 and 218 near the email-address wording), and 邮件 for messages. Make the same choice everywhere in the file the PR touched, and keep the change limited to wording.

findings.title: "Subscription details" now translated
findings.body:
The empty `"Subscription details": ""` entry in ghost.json now has the value `订阅详情`. Empty values fall back to English at runtime, so this fills a real gap for zh users. It also matches the 订阅 wording used elsewhere in the same file.

findings.title: 会籍 replaced by 订阅 for subscription wording
findings.body: The switch from 会籍 (a Traditional-Chinese-leaning term) to 订阅 in ghost.json (for example `Manage subscription` -> `管理订阅` on line 28, and `Your subscription has expired.` -> `您的订阅已过期。`) matches mainland usage, which is the PR's stated goal. The change is applied consistently across the subscription strings in that file.
